To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) we develop algorithms to generate effective hints that are more accurate than state-of-the-art approaches; (b) we develop a new sequence-based statistic that predicts student performance; (c) we demonstrate that our algorithms can be used to generate hints that are highly predictive of a learner's success.
we can autonomously generate hints by inferring problem solving policies and that these policies can be used to predict student performance.

we have developed a new method of generating hints that is more accurate than state-of-the-art approaches and we discovered a novel sequence-based statistic that is predictive of future student success.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: how can we use the patterns of student behavior to improve the learning experience?
the problem of inferring the problem solving policies of an expert teacher and using these policies to improve learning.
the question: how can we use data to help students learn more effectively?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the framework that motivates the algorithms is itself a powerful learning tool.
we are able to predict the best way to help a learner, and we can predict the success of the learner based on how we do it.
the sequence of actions that a student takes in a problem solving task is predictive of their future success and the same framework can be used to generate effective hints.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel framework for generating hints, which is also useful for predicting student success.
we have developed a framework that can predict both the way a teacher would help a student, and the way that students will succeed or fail.
the same statistical framework can be used to generate hints for a student, and also to identify students who will benefit from hints.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can leverage historical student data to develop algorithms that generate hints and identify students at risk.
the sequence of steps a learner takes can be used to predict the way a teacher might help that student, and to predict how well that student is likely to do.
by observing the sequence of steps a learner takes to solve a problem, we can infer the learner's problem solving policy and use that to generate hints and measure the learner's success.
